readings.section: The Divided Kingdom: Israel and Judah
readings.subsection: The Reign of Amaziah in Judah
readings.title: Amaziah's Reign and Victory Over Edom
readings.subtitle: He did what was right, but not like his father David.
readings.text: [2 Kings 14:1] In the second year of Yo’ash son of Yo’aḥaz, sovereign of Yisra’ěl, Amatsyahu son of Yo’ash, sovereign of Yehuḏah, began to reign. [2] He was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Yerushalayim. And his mother’s name was Yeho‛addin of Yerushalayim. [3] And he did what was right in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, but not like his father Daviḏ. He did according to all his father Yo’ash did. [4] However, the high places were not taken away. The people still slaughtered and burned incense on the high places. [5] And it came to be, as soon as the reign was strengthened in his hand, that he struck <dn>את</dn> his servants who had stricken <dn>את</dn> his father the sovereign. [6] But he did not put to death the children of the strikers, according to what is written in the Book of the Torah of Mosheh, in which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> commanded, saying, <dq>“Fathers are not put to death for the children, and children are not put to death for the fathers, but each one is put to death for his own sin.”</dq> [7] He struck <dn>את</dn> Eḏom in the Valley of Salt, ten thousand, and took <dn>את</dn> Sela in battle, and called <dn>את</dn> its name Yoqthe’ěl to this day.

readings.section: The Divided Kingdom: Israel and Judah
readings.subsection: The Reign of Amaziah in Judah
readings.title: Amaziah's Pride and Defeat
readings.subtitle: The thistle challenges the cedar, and Judah is smitten by Israel.
readings.text: [2 Kings 14:8] Amatsyah then sent messengers to Yeho’ash son of Yeho’aḥaz, son of Yěhu, sovereign of Yisra’ěl, saying, “Come, let us look each other in the face!” [9] And Yeho’ash sovereign of Yisra’ěl sent to Amatsyahu sovereign of Yehuḏah, saying, “The thistle that was in Leḇanon sent to the cedar that was in Leḇanon, saying, ‘Give your daughter to my son as wife.’ And a wild beast that was in Leḇanon passed by and trampled <dn>את</dn> the thistle. [10] “You have certainly stricken <dn>את</dn> Eḏom, and your heart has lifted you up. Be esteemed and stay in your house. But why do you stir up yourself to evil, that you should fall – you and Yehuḏah with you?” [11] But Amatsyahu did not listen, so Yeho’ash sovereign of Yisra’ěl went up, and he and Amatsyahu sovereign of Yehuḏah faced one another at Běyth Shemesh, which belongs to Yehuḏah. [12] And Yehuḏah was smitten before Yisra’ěl, and they each fled to his tent. [13] And Yeho’ash sovereign of Yisra’ěl caught <dn>את</dn> Amatsyahu sovereign of Yehuḏah, son of Yeho’ash, son of Aḥazyahu, at Běyth Shemesh. And they came to Yerushalayim and he broke through the wall of Yerushalayim from the Gate of Ephrayim to the Corner Gate, four hundred cubits, [14] and took <dn>את</dn> all the gold and silver, and <dn>את</dn> all the objects that were found in the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and in the treasuries of the sovereign’s house, and <dn>את</dn> hostages, and returned to Shomeron.

readings.section: The Divided Kingdom: Israel and Judah
readings.subsection: The Reign of Jehoash in Israel
readings.title: The Death of Jehoash, King of Israel
readings.subtitle: His acts and might are recorded in the annals.
readings.text: [2 Kings 13:12] And the rest of the acts of Yo’ash, and all that he did, and his might with which he fought against Amatsyah sovereign of Yehuḏah, are they not written in the book of the annals of the sovereigns of Yisra’ěl? [13] So Yo’ash slept with his fathers. And Yaroḇ‛am sat on his throne. And Yo’ash was buried in Shomeron with the sovereigns of Yisra’ěl.

readings.section: The Divided Kingdom: Israel and Judah
readings.subsection: The Reign of Jehoash in Israel
readings.title: Summary of Jehoash's Acts
readings.subtitle: He slept with his fathers and Jeroboam his son reigned in his place.
readings.text: [2 Kings 14:15] And the rest of the acts of Yeho’ash which he did, and his might, and how he fought with Amatsyahu sovereign of Yehuḏah, are they not written in the book of the annals of the sovereigns of Yisra’ěl? [16] So Yeho’ash slept with his fathers, and was buried in Shomeron with the sovereigns of Yisra’ěl. And Yaroḇ‛am his son reigned in his place.

readings.section: The Divided Kingdom: Israel and Judah
readings.subsection: The Reign of Jeroboam II in Israel
readings.title: Jeroboam II Restores Israel's Borders
readings.subtitle: He did evil, yet God saved Israel through him, as prophesied by Jonah.
readings.text: [2 Kings 14:23] In the fifteenth year of Amatsyahu son of Yo’ash, the sovereign of Yehuḏah, Yaroḇ‛am son of Yo’ash, the sovereign of Yisra’ěl, began to reign in Shomeron, and reigned forty-one years. [24] And he did evil in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. <dn>He</dn> did not turn away from all the sins of Yaroḇ‛am son of Neḇat, who had made Yisra’ěl sin. [25] <dn>He</dn> restored <dn>את</dn> the border of Yisra’ěl from the entrance of Ḥamath to the Sea of the Araḇah, according to the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, which <dn>He</dn> had spoken through <dn>His</dn> servant Yonah son of Amittai, the prophet who was from Gath Ḥěpher. [26] For <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> saw <dn>את</dn> the affliction of Yisra’ěl was very bitter. And there was no one, neither shut up nor left at large, to help Yisra’ěl. [27] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had not said that <dn>He</dn> would blot out <dn>את</dn> the name of Yisra’ěl from under the heavens, but saved them by the hand of Yaroḇ‛am son of Yo’ash.

readings.section: The Divided Kingdom: Israel and Judah
readings.subsection: The Reign of Amaziah in Judah
readings.title: The Conspiracy Against Amaziah
readings.subtitle: He is killed in Lachish, and his son Azariah is made king.
readings.text: [2 Kings 14:17] And Amatsyahu son of Yo’ash, sovereign of Yehuḏah, lived fifteen years after the death of Yeho’ash son of Yeho’aḥaz, sovereign of Yisra’ěl. [18] And the rest of the acts of Amatsyahu, are they not written in the book of the annals of the sovereigns of Yehuḏah? [19] And they made a conspiracy against him in Yerushalayim, and he fled to Laḵish. And they sent after him to Laḵish and killed him there, [20] and brought him on horses, and he was buried at Yerushalayim with his fathers in the City of Daviḏ. [21] And all the people of Yehuḏah took <dn>את</dn> Azaryah, who was sixteen years old, and set him up to reign instead of his father Amatsyahu. [22] He built <dn>את</dn> Ěylath and restored it to Yehuḏah, after the sovereign slept with his fathers.

readings.section: The Divided Kingdom: Israel and Judah
readings.subsection: The Reign of Azariah (Uzziah) in Judah
readings.title: The Reign of Azariah
readings.subtitle: He did what was right, but was smitten with leprosy.
readings.text: [2 Kings 15:1] In the twenty-seventh year of Yaroḇ‛am sovereign of Yisra’ěl, Azaryah son of Amatsyah, sovereign of Yehuḏah, began to reign. [2] He was sixteen years old when he began to reign, and he reigned fifty-two years in Yerushalayim. And his mother’s name was Yeḵolyahu of Yerushalayim. [3] And he did what was right in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, according to all that his father Amatsyahu did, [4] however, the high places were not taken away. The people still slaughtered and burned incense on the high places. [5] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> smote <dn>את</dn> the sovereign, so that he was a leper until the day of his death, and he dwelt in a separate house. And Yotham son of the sovereign was over the house, ruling <dn>את</dn> the people of the land.

readings.title: Jonah Flees from the Presence of YeHoVaH
readings.subtitle: A great storm arises, and Jonah is cast into the sea.
readings.text: [Jonah 1:1] And the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came to Yonah son of Amittai, saying, [2] <dq>“Arise, go to Ninevěh, the great city, and cry out against it, for their evils have come up before <dn>Me</dn>.”</dq> [3] But Yonah rose up to flee to Tarshish from the presence of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and went down to Yapho, and found a ship going to Tarshish. And he paid the fare, and went down into it, to go with them to Tarshish from the presence of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [4] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> sent out a great wind on the sea, and there was a great storm on the sea, so that the ship was thought to be broken up. [5] And the seamen were afraid, and each one cried out to his mighty one, and threw <dn>את</dn> the cargo which was in the ship into the sea, to lighten the load. But Yonah had gone down into the lowest parts of the ship, and he lay down, and was fast asleep. [6] And the captain came to him, and said to him, “What do you mean, sleeper? Arise, cry out to your <dn>Elohim</dn>, if so be that <dn>Elohim</dn> shall think about us, so that we do not perish.” [7] And they said to each other, “Come, and let us cast lots, so that we know for whose sake this evil has come upon us.” So they cast lots, and the lot fell on Yonah. [8] So they said to him, “Please explain to us! For whose sake is this evil upon us? What is your occupation? And where do you come from? What is your country? And from what people are you?” [9] And he said to them, “<dn>I</dn> am a Hebrew. And <dn>I</dn> am fearing <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, the <dn>Elohim</dn> of the heavens, who made <dn>את</dn> the sea and <dn>את</dn> the dry land.” [10] And the men were exceedingly afraid, and said to him, “Why have you done this?” For the men knew that he fled from the presence of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, for he had informed them. [11] And they said to him, “What are we to do to you to make the sea calm for us?” For the sea was growing more stormy. [12] And he said to them, “Take me and throw me into the sea, so that the sea becomes calm for you. For <dn>I</dn> know that this great storm is because of me.” [13] However, the men rowed hard to bring the ship to land, but were unable, for the sea continued to grow more stormy against them. [14] And they cried out to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and said, “We pray, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, please, let us not perish for this man’s life, and do not lay on us innocent blood. For <dn>You</dn>, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, have done as it pleased <dn>You</dn>.” [15] Then they took <dn>את</dn> Yonah and threw him into the sea, and the sea stopped raging. [16] And the men feared <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> exceedingly, and slaughtered a slaughtering to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and made vows.

readings.title: Swallowed by a Great Fish
readings.subtitle: Jonah's prayer from the stomach of Sheol.
readings.text: [Jonah 1:17] But <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> appointed a great fish to swallow <dn>את</dn> Yonah. And Yonah was in the stomach of the fish three days and three nights. [Jonah 2:1] And Yonah prayed to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> his <dn>Elohim</dn> from the stomach of the fish. [2] And he said, “<dn>I</dn> called to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> because of my distress, and <dn>He</dn> answered me. From the stomach of She’ol <dn>I</dn> cried, and <dn>You</dn> heard my voice. [3] “For <dn>You</dn> threw me into the deep, into the heart of the seas, and the floods surrounded me. All <dn>Your</dn> breakers and <dn>Your</dn> waves passed over me. [4] “So <dn>I</dn> said, ‘<dn>I</dn> have been driven away from <dn>Your</dn> eyes. Would <dn>I</dn> ever look again toward <dn>Your</dn> set-apart Hěḵal?’ [5] “Waters encompassed me, unto life, the deep closed around me, weeds were wrapped around my head. [6] “<dn>I</dn> went down to the base of the mountains, the earth with its bars were behind me forever. But <dn>You</dn> brought up my life from the pit, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, my <dn>Elohim</dn>. [7] “When my life fainted within me, <dn>I</dn> remembered <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. And my prayer went up to <dn>You</dn>, into <dn>Your</dn> set-apart Hěḵal. [8] “Those observing false worthlessnesses forsake their own loving-commitment. [9] “But <dn>I</dn> slaughter to <dn>You</dn> with the voice of thanksgiving, <dn>I</dn> pay what <dn>I</dn> have vowed. Deliverance is of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.” [10] Then <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to the fish, and it vomited Yonah onto the dry land.

readings.title: Nineveh Repents
readings.subtitle: The city believes God, fasts, and turns from its evil way.
readings.text: [Jonah 3:1] And the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came to Yonah the second time, saying, [2] <dq>“Arise, go to Ninevěh, that great city, and proclaim to it <dn>את</dn> the message that <dn>I</dn> am speaking to you.”</dq> [3] And Yonah arose and went to Ninevěh, according to the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. Now Ninevěh was a great city before <dn>Elohim</dn>, of three day’s journey. [4] And Yonah began to go in to the city on the first day’s walk. And he cried out and said, “Yet forty days, and Ninevěh shall be overthrown!” [5] And the men of Ninevěh believed in <dn>Elohim</dn>, and proclaimed a fast, and put on sackcloth, from the greatest to the least of them. [6] And the word reached the sovereign of Ninevěh, so he arose from his throne and took off his robe, and covered himself with sackcloth and sat in ashes. [7] And he proclaimed and said throughout Ninevěh, “By decree of the sovereign and his nobles: No man or beast, herd or flock, shall taste whatever – let them not eat, let them not even drink water. [8] “But let man and beast be covered with sackcloth, and call mightily to <dn>Elohim</dn>. And let each one turn from his evil way and from the violence that is in his hands. [9] “Who knows whether <dn>Elohim</dn> does turn and relent, and shall turn away from the heat of <dn>His</dn> displeasure, so that we do not perish?” [10] And <dn>Elohim</dn> saw <dn>את</dn> their works, that they turned from their evil way. And <dn>Elohim</dn> relented from the evil which <dn>He</dn> had said <dn>He</dn> would do to them, and <dn>He</dn> did not do it.

readings.title: Jonah's Displeasure
readings.subtitle: God teaches Jonah about His compassion for Nineveh.
readings.text: [Jonah 4:1] But it greatly displeased Yonah, and he was grieved. [2] And he prayed to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and he said, “Please, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, was this not what <dn>I</dn> said while <dn>I</dn> was in my own land? This is why <dn>I</dn> went ahead and fled to Tarshish. For <dn>I</dn> know that <dn>You</dn> are an <dn>Ěl</dn> showing favour, and compassionate, patient and of great loving-commitment, and relenting from doing evil. [3] “And now, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, please take <dn>את</dn> my life from me, for it is better for me to die than to live!” [4] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said, <dq>“Are you right to be displeased?”</dq> [5] Then Yonah went out of the city and sat on the east side of the city, and made himself a shelter there, and sat under it in the shade, to see what would become of the city. [6] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> appointed a plant and made it come up over Yonah, to be a shade for his head to deliver him from his discomfort. And Yonah greatly rejoiced over the plant. [7] But as morning dawned the next day <dn>Elohim</dn> appointed a worm which struck <dn>את</dn> the plant so that it withered. [8] And it came to be when the sun came up, that <dn>Elohim</dn> appointed a scorching east wind, and the sun struck on Yonah’s head, so that he grew faint, and asked for <dn>את</dn> his life to die, and said, “It is better for me to die than to live.” [9] And <dn>Elohim</dn> said to Yonah, <dq>“Have you rightly become displeased over the plant?”</dq> And he said, “<dn>I</dn> have rightly become displeased, even to death!” [10] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said, <dq>“<dn>You</dn> felt sorry for the plant for which you have not laboured, nor made it grow, which came up in a night and perished in a night.</dq> [11] <dq>“And should <dn>I</dn> not pardon Ninevěh, that great city, in which are more than one hundred and twenty thousand beings who have not known their right hand from their left, and much cattle?”</dq>
